display_name: Puerto Rico (San Juan & the Spanish Virgins)
tagline: Where a notorious daily ferry failure meets US-citizen commuters — the clearest public-transit case in the Caribbean.
summary: Puerto Rico pairs a major metro (San Juan) with the 'Spanish Virgin Islands' — Vieques and Culebra — reached from Ceiba/Fajardo by a ferry system whose chronic cancellations and overcrowding are a long-running public scandal for the US-citizen residents who depend on it. That makes PR a rare Caribbean node where the public-transport-authority case is as strong as the tourism case. San Juan itself anchors cruise and resort demand, and PR sits ~75–80 nm from the USVI, a natural Quanta-LR link into the Virgin Islands network.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns the eastern PR network — Fajardo↔Vieques (~8 nm) and ↔Culebra (~12 nm), San Juan↔Fajardo coastal (~30 nm), and the Fajardo day-cays — directly addressing the failing resident ferry.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) adds the regional links: San Juan↔USVI (~78 nm) and the run toward the Dominican Republic (~180 nm).

competitive_landscape: The ATM/HMS public ferry to Vieques and Culebra is the incumbent — and its chronic failure is precisely the opportunity. Small inter-island air (Cape Air, Vieques Air Link) and private launches fill gaps. There is no foiling incumbent; this is a public-service-quality story as much as a tourism one.
seasonality: Atlantic hurricane season (Jun–Nov) is the constraint; PR's east coast and the Vieques/Culebra channels are relatively sheltered, supporting a long Pioneer II operating window. Winter is peak tourism.
regulatory_note: US jurisdiction (USCG Subchapter T; Jones Act considerations for any US-build/flag requirements on domestic routes). The public-service angle opens FTA/federal transit and PR-government procurement channels distinct from pure tourism — and federal clean-transit funding aligns with a zero-emission fleet.
key_partners: Waldorf El Conquistador / Puerto del Rey
